summary: A Slack OAuth app lets users connect their Slack account so an agent or integration can act in their workspaces. For development, Composio's managed Slack app removes the need to register your own app, but any production app with custom branding, custom scopes, or a dedicated rate limit needs your own app registered in Slack's developer portal.

verdict.headline: Slack is self-serve for your own workspace; reaching other workspaces is possible without review, but if you want Marketplace listing or unthrottled conversation-history reads, budget for a multi-month review.
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: About 30 to 60 minutes if you have a Slack login with app-creation access and a Composio account (estimate, not sourced).
verdict.timeToProduction: Without Marketplace listing: days to about two weeks of setup, with no provider review wait, but conversation-history reads are capped at 1 request per minute. With Marketplace listing: 10+ active workspaces must exist first, then up to 10 business days for preliminary review and up to 10 weeks for functional review, so roughly 3 months at Slack's stated maximums, plus time to reach 10 workspaces.
verdict.activeEffort: Roughly 6 to 10 hands-on hours for a development app plus a production package (estimate, not sourced).
verdict.approvalWait: Marketplace listing only: up to 10 business days (preliminary) plus up to 10 weeks (functional) for new submissions, per Slack's official review guide. No approval wait is documented for distributing a non-listed app.

composio.guidance: You can build and test on Composio's managed Slack app today. Switch to your own Slack app before production if you need consent-screen branding (removing 'Composio wants to access your account'), custom scopes, or a dedicated rate-limit quota. Composio's docs conflict on whether dev-only use needs your own credentials, so confirm this in the Composio dashboard before you rely on the managed app.

prerequisites.item: A Slack account that can create apps at api.slack.com/apps
prerequisites.why: The app creation page requires sign-in; the page is public but creating an app is login-gated.
New apps are created from scratch and must pick a development workspace. Undistributed apps run on that single workspace.

prerequisites.item: A Composio project with access to the Slack auth config
prerequisites.why: You need the Composio callback URL and must enter your Slack client ID and secret if you move off the managed app.

prerequisites.item: A public HTTPS website, privacy policy, and support channel
prerequisites.why: Required for any Marketplace listing and for apps distributed to other workspaces. Support is expected to respond within 2 business days.

prerequisites.item: Test account credentials and an install path for Slack's reviewers
prerequisites.why: Slack cannot access workspaces, including ones created for testing, so you must supply a way to install the app yourself.

prerequisites.item: Legal entity, business verification, paid plan, or developer-program membership
prerequisites.why: Not determined. The pages reviewed did not state these requirements, so confirm before committing.

stages.title: Create the Slack app
stages.goal: A Slack app exists in your development workspace with the Slack client ID and client secret available.

steps.text: Sign in at https://api.slack.com/apps with your Slack account.
steps.detail: The page is public but app creation requires login. Sign in with the account that owns the development workspace.

steps.text: Click Create New App, choose From scratch, enter an app name, and select your development workspace.
steps.detail: This creates an undistributed app. It works fully in that one workspace but cannot be distributed to other workspaces.

steps.text: Note the Client ID and Client Secret from the app's Basic Information page.
steps.detail: You will enter these in the Composio auth config if you use your own app.

stages.title: Configure OAuth, scopes, and Composio
stages.goal: The app's redirect URL matches Composio's callback, requested scopes are set, and the Composio auth config points at your app.

steps.text: Add Composio's callback URL as an OAuth redirect URL under OAuth & Permissions.
steps.detail: Use the exact callback shown in the Composio dashboard. The dossier's probe used https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback, but the v3 vs v3.1 value is unverified, so copy it from Composio. Redirect URLs must use SSL.

steps.text: Draft the bot and user scope list, with a one-line justification for each scope.
steps.detail: Start with channels:read and chat:write. Avoid admin, identity, search:read, and user-token *:history scopes, which Slack says it is unlikely to approve for non-partners. Justifications are required per scope in any Marketplace submission.

steps.text: Enter the scope list in the app's OAuth & Permissions page, then reinstall the app to the development workspace.
steps.detail: Scope changes after Marketplace approval need resubmission, so settle the list now.

steps.text: Enter the Slack client ID and secret in the Composio auth config for Slack.
steps.detail: Only needed if you are moving off the managed app. Composio's docs conflict on dev vs prod credentials, so confirm in the dashboard.

steps.text: Draft the privacy policy, landing page copy, and support contact.
steps.detail: The privacy policy must state what data is collected, how it is used, and how long it is kept. You host and publish these.

stages.title: Test the install and connection
stages.goal: Your own Slack account connects through Composio and the consent screen behaves as expected.

steps.text: Install the app to your development workspace and connect your own account through Composio.
steps.detail: Check that the consent screen shows the scopes you requested. On the managed app it will read 'Composio wants to access your account'.

steps.text: Test a conversation-history read on the connected account.
steps.detail: If you distribute the app outside the Marketplace, history reads created after May 29, 2025 are limited to 1 request per minute. Custom internal apps get 50+ per minute. Plan tests around this difference.

steps.text: Record a short demo video showing install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use, and uninstall.
steps.detail: Required for any Marketplace submission. The video must include uninstallation.

stages.title: Decide distribution and submit if listing
stages.goal: Either the app is distributed without listing and you accept the history cap, or the Marketplace review is passed.
stages.duration: 4 to 8 hours + up to 10 business days preliminary + up to 10 weeks functional review (listing only)

steps.text: Decide whether to list on the Slack Marketplace or distribute without listing.
steps.detail: Listing needs 10+ active workspaces in the past 28 days. Non-listed distributed apps get the 1-per-minute history limit. Marketplace apps are not affected by that limit.

steps.text: If listing, submit the app with install and test credentials, the video demo, and scope justifications.
steps.detail: Slack will not test in your workspaces. Resubmitting during preliminary review resets your queue position. Expect follow-up questions and security review.

steps.text: If listing, prepare the submission package (justifications, privacy policy, support details) and check it against the submission checklist.
steps.detail: Draft and check only. You submit.

steps.text: Go live for end users by enabling distribution in Manage Distribution.
steps.detail: Complete all items on the distribution checklist before enabling it.

blockers.title: Marketplace submission blocked by workspace count
blockers.symptom: You cannot submit for review because the app has not been installed on 10 or more active workspaces in the past 28 days.
blockers.workaround: Either build up installs first, or skip Marketplace listing and distribute without it, accepting the conversation-history limit.

blockers.title: conversations.history throttled to 1 request per minute
blockers.symptom: Conversation-history reads from a non-Marketplace distributed app created after May 29, 2025 (or a net-new install) are limited to 1 request per minute.
blockers.workaround: Apply for Marketplace listing, use the Events API (capped at 30,000 deliveries per workspace per app per 60 minutes) instead of polling, or limit history reads per workspace.

blockers.title: Scope rejected for lack of justification
blockers.symptom: Review returns the app with a request for better reasons on requested OAuth scopes.
blockers.workaround: Write a specific justification for each scope, tied to a user-visible feature. Drop scopes you do not need.

blockers.title: Review returned for bugs or poor experience
blockers.symptom: Slack returns the submission because of bugs, poor user experience, or repeated low-quality issues.
blockers.workaround: Fix the reported issues and resubmit. Resubmitting during preliminary review resets queue position.

blockers.title: Socket Mode enabled blocks distribution
blockers.symptom: A pre-submission audit says Socket Mode apps cannot be distributed at all.
blockers.workaround: Confirm in Slack's own docs before relying on this. If Socket Mode is on and you want to distribute, turn it off and use Request URLs over SSL.

blockers.title: Redirect URL mismatch with Composio callback
blockers.symptom: The OAuth redirect fails or is rejected because the redirect URL in Slack does not match the Composio callback.
blockers.workaround: Copy the callback from the Composio dashboard exactly. The v3 vs v3.1 value is unverified in the sources.

nuances.text: Slack's rate-limit effective date for existing installs conflicts across sources (September 2, 2025 vs March 3, 2026). Plan for the later date.
Apps that provide only an MCP server without meaningful in-Slack functionality are unsuitable for listing, and Slack data may not be used to train LLMs.
You cannot email users who install the app without their explicit consent.
Once approved, the live version is locked. Scope changes need resubmission, and a staging app with identical scopes is needed for review.
Community reports conversations.history returns only about 15 messages for capped apps even with limit set higher. This is not confirmed by Slack's docs.
